A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Temporal Variational Implicit Neural Representations by the same authors. All 22 pages of v1 and 36 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, equations and figures, support comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original imputation, forecasting, downstream HAR classification and computational timing experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, multivariate forecasting, ablations, uncertainty evaluation and missing-history experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the stated training rule from minimizing to maximizing the same ELBO. The Transformer, latent-variable, hypernetwork and INR pipeline remains intact. Newly specified Laplace outputs and covariate binning clarify implementation; they do not establish a redesigned method or rerun of existing experiments.

E1.justification: The underlying datasets are retained, but v2 adds joint multivariate forecasting on Electricity, Traffic and Solar-H, requiring multiple series to be modeled together (Section 4.1.5). Appendix B.3 also adds Electricity forecasting with partially observed history, extending the previously fully observed forecasting scenario.

E2.justification: CSDI is added to univariate and multivariate imputation comparisons and downstream HAR classification. Appendix A.13 introduces evaluated TV-VAE decoder baselines, while A.8 adds a TimeFlow variant trained with randomly sampled observation ratios. The original comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: Existing splits and principal univariate settings are retained. Added protocols include enlarged networks for joint forecasting, randomized TimeFlow training, decoder and likelihood controls, and NLL/90% coverage evaluation. Missing-history forecasting uses shared test masks but different training exposure: TV-INRs receives a missing-history curriculum while baselines train on full histories. B.3 lists a 0.2 observation ratio where Table 29 lists 0.3.

E4.justification: v2 adds Fourier-frequency ablations, comparisons against direct MLP decoders, predictive calibration analysis, forecasting-error histograms, missing-history robustness tests and Laplace-versus-Gaussian sensitivity analysis (A.12–A.13 and B.1–B.4). These test architectural necessity and failure mechanisms beyond v1's existing covariate and TimeFlow missingness analyses.

E5.justification: v2 introduces quantitative predictive-uncertainty evaluation, explicitly labeled 5th–95th percentile bands and detailed best-model-versus-comparator significance tables. Welch's test at alpha=0.05 was already documented in v1. Conversely, v1's explicit three-training-seed statement disappears; this is a loss of reporting detail, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: The original main benchmark values are retained, while substantial new results cover CSDI, joint forecasting, ablations, calibration, missing-history robustness and imputation latency. Small existing values also change: TimeFlow's Electricity MAE at L=2000, training ratio 1.0 and testing ratio 0.5 changes from 0.25084 to 0.25284 (v1 Table 11; v2 Table 13). New Table 33 marks sparse-P12 comparisons of C-TV-INRs against SAITS and TV-INRs as nonsignificant, unlike v1's significant-superiority claim.

T1.justification: Appendix A.9 adds componentwise complexity reasoning under the assumption L is much larger than embedding and latent dimensions, yielding stated time and memory bounds of O(NL²E) and O(ML²). v2 also removes the earlier equality that incorrectly defined the absent-index set as all indices. These are bounded analytical additions and corrections, without new central theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central probabilistic-INR, individualized prediction and single-training claims remain. The abstract narrows comparisons to existing INR approaches and qualifies order-of-magnitude improvements as occurring on several datasets. The conclusion replaces the broad inference-efficiency advantage with the more specific claim of fixed inference time independent of gradient adaptation.

C2.justification: v1 already discussed stronger competitors in some settings and long-horizon outliers. v2 substantially extends interpretation through architectural-complexity tradeoffs, calibration behavior, decoder and likelihood explanations, and explicit limitations concerning informative missingness and a single global latent representation. It also distinguishes evaluated in-distribution generalization from unevaluated foundation-model and out-of-distribution settings.

D1.justification: v2 adds an anonymous code link and repository-based data/dependency instructions in its reproducibility statement. It newly specifies the Laplace output parameterization, covariate binning, temporal pooling, AdamW use and configurations for added experiments. The existing detailed split, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for CSDI, LSCD and temporal INR foundation models, plus references supporting missing-data mechanisms, masked training and Fourier features. This broadens and qualifies the existing research positioning without replacing its central relationship to INR, hypernetwork and amortized-inference work.

P1.justification: The introduction, contributions, related-work passages, method instructions and experimental narrative undergo substantial rewriting. v2 adds an explicit pipeline summary, reorganizes appendix material and introduces dedicated reproducibility and limitations sections. These changes materially reshape the explanation and navigation beyond simply appending results.

P2.justification: v2 expands comparison tables and the classification figure with CSDI, adds numerous analytical tables and an error-distribution figure, and redraws prediction examples with percentile bands. Main-table highlighting changes from significance/comparability to best/second-best means, the dataset summary moves to the appendix, and the document adopts journal formatting.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct validation of the INR decoder's contribution and quantitative assessment of its probabilistic predictions. v2's targeted decoder/Fourier ablations, calibration measurements and explicit failure analyses substantially strengthen architectural justification and expose applicability limits, including serious interval undercoverage. Different training curricula and inconsistent ratios weaken the missing-history comparison, and the lost seed-count statement reduces transparency, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the broader gains in validation and qualification.
